scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Full Moon Ritual of the Mundaala
This is Kangeelu. Traditional, ongoing.
on_screen: Title card: Kangeelu · India · Traditional, ongoing

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates from the Udupi and Dakshina Kannada regions of Karnataka and is performed by the Mundaala community.
It is a spiritual practice conducted during the full moon of the Tulu month of Mai to invoke protection from disease and evil.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed during the seven-day Kangilu Kunitha, the dance is a ritual to propitiate goddess Khadgeshwari and the spirit Koragajja.
It aims to foster peace, harmony, and community spirit while protecting the village from negative energy.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform in a circle, with 5 to 12 members per group.
The performance involves heavy, colorful costumes made from coconut and palm leaves, face paint, and a central masked dancer representing Koragajja.
The movement is accompanied by drumming and singing.
Watch for Koragajja impersonation.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Dancers stand in a circle.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is driven by the beats of Kaase or Dholu drums.
Four singers positioned in the center of the circle wear bells and sing traditional songs, specifically 'Karungilo' and 'Aati Kalenje'.
Listen for the Kaase, Dholu, Bells.
The music is characterized by the rhythmic percussion of Kaase or Dholu drums, accompanied by the ringing of bells worn by central singers who perform traditional folk songs.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear heavy, colorful dresses constructed from tender coconut and palm leaves.
The masked dancer representing Koragajja uses black body paint.
The performance takes place in village settings, including house visits and processions to the village outskirts.
